Subject: Pre-sales: Compact dedicated sizing worksheet & data asks

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To make the Dedicated sizing call productive, attached is a compact worksheet that collects the minimum telemetry we need to produce an initial GPU-fit recommendation and a short list of clarifying questions. If you can return the CSV export (sample telemetry) and answers below, we can put together a first-cut sizing within 48 hours.

Quick asks (short version):
- Time window: a representative 7–14 day sample (UTC preferred)
- Peak QPS and sustained QPS by hour/day
- Avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens, and 95th pct response token length
- Percent of calls that use session affinity / KV cache reuse and average session length (requests/session)
- Percent streaming completions vs non-streaming
- Any function/tool-calling usage and average call count per request

Attachments: redwood_compact_sizing_sheet.xlsx (small form), example CSV stub, MVP-MAP.pdf (mutual action plan template).

Notes: we size to meet your 95th percentile latency SLOs by default and include ~20% headroom for burst windows unless you prefer a more conservative commit.

If you prefer, we can hop on a 30-minute follow-up next week to walk through the worksheet together.

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pre-sales: Compact dedicated sizing worksheet & data asks

Hannah —

Thanks, attached is a 10k-row sample export (helios_sample_telemetry.csv). I pulled the numbers for the last 10 business days — happy to extend if you need more history.

Quick summary from our side:
- Peak observed QPS (1-min peak): 78
- Sustained average QPS (business hours): ~16
- Daily 95th pct QPS (1-min): ~62 (most spikes between 11:30–13:30 UTC)
- Avg prompt tokens: 140 tokens
- Avg response tokens: 420 tokens
- Avg tokens per request: ~560 tokens
- 95th pct response token length: 1,800 tokens (long-form reports; ~6% of calls)
- Session affinity / KV cache reuse: ~28% of user journeys reuse a session; average requests/session: 5.4
- Streaming completions: ~55% of responses use streaming (primarily UX where progress is shown)
- Function/tool calling: ~12% of requests invoke 1–2 external tools (web fetch, DB lookup)

Constraints / asks:
- We need predictable latency for interactive flows (P99 <= 900ms) and can tolerate slower throughput for batch report generation (these are usually asynchronous).
- We expect growth ~2.2x over next 9 months and want guidance on staged capacity.

Let us know if these numbers are sufficient — otherwise I can run a full export.

—Evan
Evan Cho
Head of Platform Engineering | Helios Labs
evan@helioslabs.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cho <evan@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-sales: Compact dedicated sizing worksheet & data asks

Evan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the sample. A few clarification points so our sizing assumptions align with Helios expectations:

1) The 78 QPS 1-min peak — is that dominated by short transactional requests (prompt+small response) or the long-form generation traffic? If you can, mark the rows in the CSV with a "use_case" tag (transactional | long_gen) or confirm approximate split.

2) For the 95th pct response length (1,800 tokens) — what's the typical concurrency for those long requests? Are they usually single-user background jobs or do they happen concurrently across many users?

3) For streaming — is streaming used end-to-end (client opens streaming socket) or do you fall back to non-streaming when network conditions are poor? This affects memory/KV cache strategies.

4) For function/tool-calling — are tool responses counted in your response token numbers or do they appear as separate downstream calls?

Initial sizing heuristic (informal, for discussion): given the mix you shared, we would model two traffic regimes:
- Interactive surface (80% of calls): aim for low-latency instances, use continuous batching with small batch windows; approximate sizing target: support sustained 20 QPS at p95 latency constraints with headroom,
- Long-generation cohort (10%–12% of calls): size for throughput/slotting and prioritized queueing; these can run on separate pool(s) optimized for memory (larger GPU RAM / fewer concurrent sessions).

Early suggestion: run a 2-tier reserved pool: a low-latency pool for interactive at lower GPU occupancy, plus a high-memory batch pool for long-gen. We can convert these into a 90-day staged commit with burst capacity. We'll map to specific GPU SKUs after we validate the CSV splits and tail concurrency numbers.

If it's helpful, we can propose an initial GPU mix (e.g., 4 x A100-40GB for interactive + 3 x A100-80GB for long-gen) but want to confirm the concurrency of long requests first.

Would you be available for a 30-minute sizing call today at 3pm PT or Thursday?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Pre-Sales Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Evan —

Thanks for the detail and the CSV. Next steps (mutual action plan):

1) Helios: add a "use_case" tag where possible in the CSV (transactional | long_gen) and confirm whether the 1,800-token long calls are mostly single-threaded background jobs or concurrent interactive reports. Target by EOD Wed.
2) Redwood: we'll run a traffic decomposition using the sample and return an initial GPU-fit proposal (SKU mix and estimated committed pool) + expected latency curves by Thu COB.
3) Legal / Procurement: Hannah will share the initial term sheet and burst/fallback language; Helios procurement to provide required billing/contact info.

Proposed timeline: sizing call (walkthrough): Thu 07/16 10:00 AM PT; deliver initial sizing brief: Thu 07/16 COB; follow-on architecture workshop (optional): week of 7/20.

I've linked the HubSpot deal and uploaded the MAP to Drive: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/HELIOS-8927 and https://drive.google.com/open?id=0B_example_drive_link

Ben and Karthik — looping you both for visibility on the GPU mix and any redlines on headroom assumptions.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
